schemes.description: Compulsory first-year interdisciplinary course (themes in 2025/26: climate futures, controlling AI, fair society). In Winter Term students work in seminar-allocated groups of 4-5 to analyse a system and propose a change, written up as a policy proposal addressed to governmental/institutional actors or a strategic plan for a social movement/activist organisation, delivered as a group digital report and a seminar presentation. The 'target audience' is chosen within the brief; no evidence that an external organisation sets the brief, receives the output or assesses it.
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: All first-year LSE undergraduates (not postgraduates). Counts as one half-unit-equivalent first-year mark (not towards classification for LLB).
schemes.credit_assessment: Half-unit equivalent. 2025/26 LSE100A: critical evaluation 50% (1,000 words) + project 50% (3,000 words). 2024 policy: group project mark = presentation 25% + digital report 75%; single group mark.
schemes.duration: Autumn and Winter Terms; group project over Winter Term
schemes.project_evidence: Group research project with defined task (analyse a system, propose a policy proposal or strategic plan) and identifiable outputs: digital report and presentation [1][2][3].
schemes.group_evidence: Groups of 4-5 students allocated by seminar teacher; single group mark for joint digital report and presentation [1][2].
schemes.employer_evidence: Proposal is written 'for a target audience' (governmental/institutional actors or a social movement/activist organisation) defined within the course brief; no source shows an external organisation supplying a brief, receiving outputs or assessing. Assessed by seminar teachers [1][2]. Marked No on the positive evidence of an academically set, audience-addressed (hypothetical client) design; would change only if a cohort-specific partner is evidenced.
schemes.unresolved: Whether any individual LSE100 themes involve external organisations as audiences/judges (Moodle-only material).

sources.title: LSE100 Assessment
sources.extract: Group project by teams of 4-5 over Winter Term; 'The change students identify will take the form of either a policy proposal addressing governmental or institutional actors within the system, or a strategic plan for a social movement or activist organisation to enact change.' 'Students collaboratively produce a digital report and presentation outlining their proposed change for a target audience.'

sources.extract: Groups allocated by the seminar teacher in late Autumn Term based on topic preference and disciplinary diversity; mark split presentation (25%) and digital report (75%); each group receives a single group mark.

schemes.description: International online experiential programme delivered by QS with a consortium of universities and promoted to LSE students via the LSE100 pages. LSE undergraduates join international teams of about five students (with 1-2 academic mentors) for ~12 weeks to work on a UN SDG challenge set by a business, charity or NGO partner, ending in a solutions showcase.
schemes.admin_host: LSE100 (LSE recruitment) / QS and international university consortium (delivery)
schemes.year_of_study: Any undergraduate year (not restricted in evidence)
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Open to all LSE undergraduates via application; criteria: interest in SDGs, collaboration/communication, leadership potential, analytical skills.
schemes.credit_assessment: No evidence of credit; described as accessible 'alongside your studies' (probably extracurricular).
schemes.duration: ~12 weeks; LSE recruits two cohorts per academic year
schemes.project_evidence: Teams address a specific sustainability challenge set by a partner and present solutions at the Future17 Solution Showcase [1].
schemes.group_evidence: Students work in teams of about five with students from other universities, each team with 1-2 academic mentors [1].
schemes.employer_evidence: Challenges are set by global organisations (business, charity or NGO partners); students work with the partner on its SDG challenge [1].
schemes.partner_role: Sets live challenge; works with team; receives solutions at showcase
schemes.deliverable: Solution/recommendations presented at Future17 Solution Showcase
schemes.unresolved: Credit status; number of LSE participants; named partner organisations for LSE cohorts; whether the September 2026 call is for the autumn 2026 cohort (assumed).

sources.title: Future17: Join a global team solving real sustainability challenges
sources.extract: 'an international experiential learning programme that brings together students from leading universities around the world to tackle real sustainability challenges set by global organisations'; runs approx. 12 weeks, delivered entirely online; teams of about five with one or two academic mentors working with a business, charity or NGO partner on an SDG challenge; 'Applications are open to all LSE undergraduate students'; applications close 7 September 2026; LSE recruits two cohorts each academic year.

schemes.description: LSE Volunteer Centre consultancy challenge: student teams (reported as 6-7 students) act as volunteer consultants to UK or overseas charities, investigating a charity-set problem (e.g. fundraising strategy, attracting younger audiences, inclusivity, marketing strategy), liaising with the charity as client and delivering a consultancy report and presentation, supported by an LSE alumni mentor.

schemes.project_evidence: Teams answer a charity's project brief and produce actionable recommendations in consultancy reports and presentations [1][2].

schemes.employer_evidence: Charities apply with project briefs, act as clients with whom teams liaise, and receive the consultancy report/presentation [1][2][3].
schemes.partner_role: Client: sets brief, liaises with team, receives report/presentation
schemes.deliverable: Consultancy report and presentation to the charity
schemes.participation_data: Team size 6-7 students reported in Volunteer Centre blog posts (2023-2024); number of teams/charities not published in sources found.

profile_md:
**LSE** has substantial but mainly **postgraduate, programme-embedded** live-client group project provision, together with a few institution-wide extracurricular routes.

- **Institution-wide:** **LSE100** is compulsory for all first-year undergraduates and includes a 4-5 person group research project. That project is addressed to a self-defined target audience, and no external organisation was evidenced, so it is a near-miss on criterion C. The open qualifying routes are selective and extracurricular: **Future17** (QS consortium; teams of about five work on SDG challenges set by business, charity or NGO partners; open to all undergraduates), the **Volunteer Centre Community Engagement Programme** (teams of 6-7 work as consultants on charity briefs; open to all students) and the **Research Volunteering Scheme** (postgraduate teams answer charity research questions; 10 questions in 2025/26).
- **Embedded client capstones (compulsory within programmes):**
  - **Management:** a sponsored Business Projects framework (GMiM MG488B, CEMS, HRO Links in pairs, MSc Marketing MG4F1), the MiM capstone MG4J4 / London Consulting Project, and the SIE partner project MG4G6.
  - **School of Public Policy:** the MPA capstone PP4B3, where the client marks 20%; also PP4B5 and the Executive MPP capstone PP4B3E with the Civil Service.
  - **International Development:** the DV443, DV453 and DV466 consultancy projects with clients such as UN agencies and NGOs.
  - **Statistics:** the ST498 Data Science capstone, co-supervised by industry partners.
  - **Undergraduate:** the only curricular undergraduate route verified is the **GV343 PPE Capstone** (year 4), with an external client and a report to that client.
- **Partners:** clients define the problems, co-supervise, receive the reports and presentations, and sometimes assess.
- **Uncertain:** credit for Future17; the current status of the law clinics; group size in MA425; whether live clients are used in GY454; and possible further departmental instances (Economics, Social Policy and Media had none found).
gaps: Future17 credit status and LSE participant numbers; Department of Management 'Open Innovation' business-project stream and SIE consulting capstone not identified at course level; CEMS/MBA project credit and which 'MBA' students; PP4B5/PP4B3E assessment and compulsory status; PP4A7E Urban Consultancy Project (Executive MSc Cities) not searched in detail; LAC Policy Clinic (reports on live issues for external partners) not separately verified; law clinic current cohorts undated; no client-project evidence found for Economics, Social Policy, Media & Communications, Psychological & Behavioural Science, Anthropology, Sociology, International Relations, Accounting, Finance (not every department searched individually; further departmental instances may exist); search budget exceeded (42 searches) to calibrate depth.
